solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Trendy little brother screens vacuous chick flick (8,4)

indicatorNotes.screens: to screen something is to hide it behind or inside you, so BRO goes round RIGHT ON
indicatorNotes.vacuous: a vacuous chick has nothing inside, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: bro is the short form of brother

annotation.surface: A trendy kid brother puts on a mindless romcom for the family.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chick flick" looks like one phrase, but only "flick" (film) defines: Brighton Rock is the Graham Greene story filmed in 1947.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Graham Greene thriller was filmed in 1947, and flick is slang for any film.

entries.clue: York yobbo carrying weapon launcher (4,3)

indicatorNotes.carrying: in a down clue, the yobbo carries the weapon on top of him, so BOW sits above LOUT

blocks.note: a yobbo is a loutish youth

annotation.surface: A thug from the city of York is caught toting a rocket launcher.
annotation.walkthrough: York looks like the city, but in cricket to york a batsman is to dismiss him with a yorker, a ball pitched at his feet; to bowl out is to dismiss a batsman.
annotation.definitionFit: A cricket sense: a yorker, pitched right at the batsman's toes, often knocks over the stumps, so york is a specific way of dismissing him.

entries.clue: Much-loved engine, creamy white, leaving yard (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the yard letter leaves the word

blocks.note: ivory is a creamy white colour

annotation.surface: A treasured steam engine loses its cream paint as it pulls out of the yard.
annotation.walkthrough: Ivor the Engine is a much-loved British children's TV cartoon about a little Welsh steam locomotive.
annotation.definitionFit: Ivor the Engine is the beloved locomotive of the children's series.

entries.clue: Journalist eating flipping strange fish (7)

indicatorNotes.eating: the journalist takes the other piece inside
indicatorNotes.flipping: ODD is turned over to DDO

blocks.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist

annotation.surface: A reporter tucks into a thoroughly peculiar fish supper.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flipping" reads as a mild British expletive modifying "strange", but it is the instruction to turn ODD round.
annotation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish.

entries.clue: Lowly degree accepted by Oxford University “concerning” (7)

indicatorNotes.accepted by: the degree is taken in by OU

annotation.surface: A modest degree gets taken up by Oxford, which is worrying.
annotation.walkthrough: "Lowly" looks like an adjective for the degree, but it is the definition: obscure in the sense of humble, as in obscure origins.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone of obscure birth is lowly, unknown and humble.

entries.clue: Stones casting off clothing in wild party (4)

indicatorNotes.casting off clothing: the word's outer layer, its first and last letters, is taken off

blocks.note: gravel = small stones; strip G and L

annotation.surface: Rolling Stones fans strip off at a riotous party.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital S makes "Stones" look like the band, but it is just small stones.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the word names a large, loud, all-night dance event.

entries.clue: 4 Down caught on one occasion AWOL on vacation (7)

annotation.definitionNote: 4 Down is OBSCURE, here read as a verb

indicatorNotes.on vacation: AWOL is vacated, emptied of its inside, leaving A…L

blocks.note: AWOL with its middle cleared out

annotation.surface: A soldier absent without leave is caught hiding somewhere during his holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 4 Down, OBSCURE, taken as a verb: to obscure something is to hide it.
annotation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it from view.

entries.clue: Actor’s debut playing Chaplin, a true star (5,8)

indicatorNotes.debut: a debut is a first appearance, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.playing: the letters are played about with

annotation.surface: An actor's first role is playing Charlie Chaplin, a genuine screen star.
annotation.walkthrough: "Star" seems to praise Chaplin, but it is literal: Alpha Centauri is the nearest star system to the Sun.
annotation.definitionFit: Alpha Centauri is the brightest star in the southern constellation Centaurus.

entries.clue: Penne tossed with caper? Yep, it’s spicy! (7,6)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a description, 'it' standing for the noun

indicatorNotes.tossed: the letters are tossed like pasta in a pan

annotation.surface: A cook tastes a pasta dish of penne tossed with capers and declares it fiery.
annotation.walkthrough: The kitchen scene makes the fodder look like a recipe, and the answer is just what you might sprinkle into that pan.
annotation.definitionFit: Cayenne pepper is a hot, spicy ground chilli.

entries.clue: American wife entertained by funny retired old judge (3,4)

indicatorNotes.entertained by: the funny word takes A and W in as guests
indicatorNotes.retired: retire = draw back, so DROLL runs backwards

annotation.surface: An American woman is amused by a witty retired judge.
annotation.walkthrough: Law lords sat in the House of Lords as Britain's highest court until the Supreme Court replaced them in 2009, hence "old".
annotation.definitionFit: A law lord was a senior judge sitting in the House of Lords.

entries.clue: In Kansas, a van navigates flatland (7)

indicatorNotes.In: the answer is in the words that follow

annotation.surface: A van drives across the prairie of Kansas.
annotation.walkthrough: The American picture of a van on the plains nearly gives it away: the answer is a flat grassland like the landscape described.
annotation.definitionFit: A savanna is a flat, grassy plain.

entries.clue: Foo Fighters’ fourth backing beat made by this? (4)

indicatorNotes.fourth: take the fourth letter of FIGHTERS
indicatorNotes.backing: backing = going backwards, so FOOH turns round

annotation.surface: The Foo Fighters' fourth album is praised for its driving backbeat.
annotation.walkthrough: The rock band is split in two: FOO as it stands and just one letter of Fighters. The question mark flags a definition by example: a hoofbeat is made by a hoof.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint rather than a synonym: the clopping of a horse's foot is named after the foot itself, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Drained jumbo drink in large bowl (5)

indicatorNotes.Drained: emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters

annotation.surface: Someone downs a giant drink served in a huge bowl.
annotation.walkthrough: A jorum is an old word for a large drinking bowl, so the drinking surface points the right way.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, though an old word: it names a big drinking vessel, often for punch.

entries.clue: Garden party price includes refreshments, we’re told? (4)

indicatorNotes.includes: the price takes the next piece inside
indicatorNotes.we’re told: the word is heard, not read, so TEA gives the letter T

blocks.note: tea sounds like the letter T

annotation.surface: The entrance fee for a garden party covers the tea and cakes.
annotation.walkthrough: A fete is a British outdoor fundraising event, typically with stalls and tea on a lawn.
annotation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor party or festival, often held in a garden.

entries.clue: Explorer books taxi first thing (5)

indicatorNotes.first thing: the taxi goes at the front

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: A traveller books a taxi for early in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: "First thing" reads as early morning, but it is a placing instruction. John Cabot sailed from Bristol to North America in 1497.
annotation.definitionFit: John Cabot was the Venetian explorer who reached Newfoundland.

entries.clue: Daughter put on fashionable island cotton fabric (5)

indicatorNotes.put on: in a down clue, D is put on top of the rest

annotation.surface: A daughter dresses in stylish island cotton.
annotation.walkthrough: "Put on" suggests getting dressed, which suits the answer, a garment, but here it only stacks the pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the cotton loincloth worn by Hindu men, and also the cloth it is made from.

entries.clue: Indian city reduced basic rations (7)

blocks.note: tack = plain food, as in hardtack, the ship's biscuit

annotation.surface: An Indian city has cut back its staple food supplies.
annotation.walkthrough: Cuttack is a major city in the Indian state of Odisha.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: it is a former capital of Odisha, in eastern India.

entries.clue: IT gazillionaire with no time for layer of command (7)

indicatorNotes.with no: a tycoon with no time is one without it, so the T of time must go from TECH ELON

blocks.note: t = time, removed from the front

annotation.surface: A tech billionaire has no time for the middle managers of his company.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a busy tycoon; the definition is the tier of management he is too busy for.
annotation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or rank in an organisation or command.

entries.clue: Channel broadcast contrary arguments (7)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: on the radio you hear the words, not their spelling

blocks.note: nah = no, the contrary answer; rows = arguments

annotation.surface: A TV channel airs a debate full of opposing points of view.
annotation.walkthrough: "Channel" looks like a TV station beside "broadcast", but it is the definition: a narrow strait of water.
annotation.definitionFit: Narrows are a narrow channel of water between two larger bodies.

entries.clue: Runs rising megastore stocking Meissen’s first new dish (7)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising = read upwards, so IKEA becomes AEKI
indicatorNotes.stocking: the megastore stocks, holds, the M
indicatorNotes.first: the first of Meissen is its opening letter, M

annotation.surface: A growing furniture megastore starts stocking Meissen porcelain.
annotation.walkthrough: Meissen is famous German porcelain, so the chinaware surface fits the answer, a small baking dish.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the small ovenproof pot for soufflés and crème brûlée is one kind of dish.

entries.clue: Second family of Hull regularly downed too much booze (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so take every second letter

annotation.surface: A second family from Hull regularly drinks far too much.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder for the alternate letters takes in "of" as well as Hull, which a solver reading Hull alone would miss. Hull is a port city in Yorkshire.
annotation.definitionFit: A skinful is as much drink as one can hold, enough to get drunk.

entries.clue: Vessel with periodically lumpy sauce (7)

blocks.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

annotation.surface: A sauceboat holds a gravy that has gone lumpy here and there.
annotation.walkthrough: "Vessel" suggests a jug or sauceboat, but it is a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the tomato condiment is the commonest sauce on a table.

entries.clue: Mr Klein’s pants seat well protected? (7)

indicatorNotes.pants: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess

annotation.surface: Calvin Klein's trousers give his seat plenty of cover.
annotation.walkthrough: The underwear designer points to pants as garments, but here it is British slang for rubbish. The Kremlin is the fortified seat of Russian government.
annotation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the walled citadel that is the seat of Russian power.

entries.clue: Chat show host upset, addressing threat to whales (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset = turned upside down, so OPRAH reads upwards

annotation.surface: A talk show host is distressed while tackling the danger facing whales.
annotation.walkthrough: HARPO is also the name of Oprah's production company, her name spelt backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A harpoon is the barbed spear used to kill whales.

entries.clue: Rounds in the morning, doctor? (4)

annotation.surface: A doctor does the ward rounds in the morning.
annotation.walkthrough: The hospital picture makes "rounds" a doctor's visits, but they are rounds of ammunition.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the military sense: a round is a single cartridge, and the clipped word covers the lot.

entries.clue: Struggles to get to grips with British atmosphere (5)

indicatorNotes.to get to grips with: the struggling word grips the B inside it

annotation.surface: Someone battles to come to terms with the mood in Britain.
annotation.walkthrough: Vibes is informal for the feeling a place gives off.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: the feeling a place or group gives off, short for vibrations.

entries.clue: Finish recording western hip-hop (4)

annotation.surface: The band finishes recording a hip-hop track in a western style.
annotation.walkthrough: "It's a wrap" is what a director says when filming or recording is finished.
annotation.definitionFit: Film and studio jargon: a director calls "that's a wrap" when a shoot or session is complete.

entries.clue: Connery’s gaffer’s nonsense (4)

indicatorNotes.Connery’s: Sean Connery famously says his s sounds as sh, so this is the word as he would say it

blocks.note: a gaffer is a foreman or boss; say it with Connery's slushy s

annotation.surface: Sean Connery's old foreman talks rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: Gaffer is British for a boss or foreman. Sean Connery's Scottish lisp, turning s into sh, is widely mimicked.
annotation.definitionFit: Bosh is dated British slang for nonsense.

entries.clue: Jelly Roll musical piece? (4)

indicatorNotes.Roll: roll the word over so it runs backwards

blocks.note: a raga is an Indian musical composition

annotation.surface: A question about Jelly Roll Morton, the jazz pianist, and one of his pieces.
annotation.walkthrough: "Jelly Roll" looks like one name, Jelly Roll Morton the jazz pianist, but it splits into definition and indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in cooking and labs.

entries.clue: Corrupt offer to trouser a thousand in dodgy cash (4-3)

indicatorNotes.to trouser: to trouser is to pocket, so OFFER takes A and K inside

annotation.surface: A crooked official offers to pocket a thousand in shady cash.
annotation.walkthrough: To trouser money is British slang for pocketing it. A rake-off is an illicit share of profits.
annotation.definitionFit: A rake-off is a share of money taken dishonestly.

entries.clue: Large cheer from crowd going round that’s horrible in the ear (7)

indicatorNotes.going round: L plus OLE surround the next piece

annotation.surface: A huge roar from the crowd grates painfully on the ear.
annotation.walkthrough: Lughole is British slang for the ear.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang synonym, from lug, an old word for the ear flap.

entries.clue: Fuse behind neon light failed eventually (2,3,4,3)

indicatorNotes.behind: RUN goes behind, after, the rest
indicatorNotes.failed: the light's letters fail and rearrange

blocks.note: to run is to melt, as metals fuse

annotation.surface: A fuse at the back of a neon sign finally blew.
annotation.walkthrough: "Failed" sits at the end as if part of the story, but it is the anagram indicator for NEON LIGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means over a long enough time, at last.
